hr_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up an applicant tracking system ({{vendor}}) account for our hiring pipeline. This step establishes a paid vendor relationship, so a human must give final approval before anything is submitted or paid for.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: our company legal name, the primary admin email/domain to use for signup, our approximate team/hiring size, and which {{vendor}} pricing plan or tier we're considering (if I haven't already told you).
2. Research and open the {{vendor}} signup/account-creation form.
3. Fill in all required fields (company name, admin contact, team size, plan selection, billing details placeholders) using the information I provided, using your configured credentials where account authentication is required.
4. Do NOT enter or submit any payment information, and do NOT click any final "create account," "subscribe," "agree to terms," or "confirm purchase" button.
5. Prepare a clear summary showing: the plan/tier selected, estimated cost, all form fields as filled, and any terms of service or contract highlights you find (renewal terms, cancellation policy, data ownership clauses).
6. Save/draft the form in whatever state {{vendor}}'s interface allows without finalizing, or if that's not possible, present me with a screenshot/copy of the completed form fields instead.

Once the draft is ready, stop for human sign-off — do not submit the form, accept any terms, approve payment, or create the account yourself. Report back with: the vendor form URL, the completed field values, the plan and estimated pricing, any contract/terms summary, and a clear note that this is awaiting my explicit approval before you or I finalize the account creation.

hr_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure interview pipeline stages in our applicant tracking system ({{vendor}}) as part of setting up our hiring ATS. 

First, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account URL/domain if not already known, (2) the job role(s) or requisition(s) I want interview stages configured for, and (3) any existing stage names, question banks, or scorecard attributes I already use, so you can reuse them rather than inventing new ones.

Then, using my configured credentials, do the following in {{vendor}}:
1. Retrieve the current recruitment pipeline stages defined in our recruiting preferences (use the dashboard or the stages-listing API) so you know what already exists.
2. Draft a proposed interview plan per role: an ordered list of pipeline stages (e.g. screen, phone interview, onsite/panel, offer), with a structured scorecard for each stage listing the specific attributes or competencies to be rated and a focus area per interviewer type.
3. Note any stages that would be net-new versus stages that already exist and just need reuse.
4. Prepare this as a clear, reviewable document (stage name, order, scorecard attributes, interviewer focus) — do not create or modify anything in {{vendor}} yet.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, you must not create, edit, or publish any stages, scorecards, or pipeline configuration in {{vendor}}. Present the full draft plan for my review and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the proposed stage list per role, the scorecard attributes per stage, which stages are new vs. reused, and any open questions (e.g. missing interviewer names or unclear rubric items) that need my input before you can finalize the draft.

hr_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me create job postings in {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking system, as part of setting up hiring pipelines. If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} account/workspace URL, (2) the specific role(s) I want posted, including title, department, seniority, location/remote policy, and salary band, and (3) any tone/voice guidance or an existing job description sample to match my style.

Using your configured credentials, do the following in {{vendor}}: draft a complete job posting for each role, including a description, responsibilities, and requirements written in my tone from the role context I gave you. Set up the application form with any custom screening questions and knockout rules I specify, and configure EEOC/demographic data collection fields per {{vendor}}'s compliant defaults. Configure the job's approval chain so it routes to me (or the designated approver) before publishing. If {{vendor}} supports job board distribution, prepare the fan-out settings (LinkedIn, Indeed, aggregators) and note any sponsored-post options, but do not activate spend without my explicit input on budget.

Save all postings as drafts/pending-approval within {{vendor}} — do not publish, activate, or distribute them. Done looks like: each job posting fully drafted with description, application form, screening questions, EEOC fields, and approval routing configured, sitting in a 'pending approval' state inside {{vendor}}.

Report back with: a list of the postings created, a link or reference to each in {{vendor}}, a summary of the approval chain configured, and any fields or decisions (e.g., salary band, sponsored posting budget) that need my confirmation. Then stop for human sign-off before anything is published or sent to job boards.

hr_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up scorecard templates in {{vendor}}, our applicant-tracking system, as part of configuring our hiring pipeline. Approval is required before any changes go live, so you must prepare everything but stop short of applying it.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: which role(s) or job requisitions need scorecards, the interview stages/plan for each role (e.g., recruiter screen, hiring manager interview, panel rounds, final), and any attributes or competencies I want scored per stage (e.g., technical depth, communication, culture add, role-specific skills).

Then, using your configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and:
1. Review the existing interview plan structure for the relevant role(s) to see which stages already exist.
2. Draft a scorecard template per stage, listing the specific attributes/competencies to be rated, a simple rubric or rating scale for each, and per-interviewer focus areas so each interviewer's scorecard is distinct (e.g., avoid duplicate questions across interviewers).
3. Draft an accompanying question bank per stage that maps to the scorecard attributes, so interviewers have consistent prompts to use.
4. Compile a clear preview/checklist showing: role name, stage, attributes per scorecard, interviewer assignments, and rating scale — organized so I can review it quickly.

Do not publish, save-as-final, or activate any scorecard template in {{vendor}} — only create drafts or leave them in an unpublished/pending state if the interface allows it. Do not assign scorecards to live interviews yet.

When done, report back with: the list of roles/stages covered, a summary of each scorecard's attributes and rubric, and any gaps or ambiguities you found (e.g., missing stages, unclear rubric scales). Then stop for human sign-off before anything is applied or activated.

hr_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me connect our {{vendor}} applicant-tracking system's hosted careers page to our company domain so job postings publish automatically with no engineering work required.

First, ask me for any of these if not already known: our company domain (or subdomain, e.g. careers.ourcompany.com), our {{vendor}} account login context (assume I use my configured credentials), and any branding assets (logo, colors, header copy) I want applied to the page.

Then do the following:
1. In {{vendor}}'s settings, locate the careers page / careers site module and review the current configuration (custom domain setup, branding, and published jobs list).
2. Prepare the custom domain connection: identify the DNS records (CNAME or equivalent) {{vendor}} requires, and draft them clearly (record type, host, value) so I can add them via my DNS provider or so you can add them if you already have DNS access via my configured credentials.
3. Apply or draft the branding settings (logo, colors, company description) in the {{vendor}} careers page editor.
4. Confirm that the job offers currently marked as published in {{vendor}} (retrievable via the offers API) are set to appear on the careers page, and that the candidate application form is correctly linked so applications submit back into {{vendor}} as candidates.
5. Prepare a short summary/checklist of: the domain/DNS changes needed, the branding applied, and the list of jobs that will go live on the page.

Because this change affects our public-facing company website, do not push the domain connection live or make it publicly visible yourself — prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the DNS records needed (if any), a link/preview of the configured careers page, the list of jobs set to publish, and a clear note on what still requires my explicit approval before going live.
